A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoLibra and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Matching relocated diagrams and retained appendix experiments supports a reliable comparison despite substantial revision of the agent-improvement section.

before.justification: v2 reports original human-validation results, coverage and redundancy experiments, a behavior-example ablation, game-agent improvement experiments, and web-agent fine-tuning results.

after.justification: v3 retains original validation and appendix experiments and reports a new Gemini-based automated prompt-optimization experiment in Section 5 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The core grounding, clustering, evaluation, and metric-optimization algorithms remain unchanged. Section 5 adds an automated prompt-update procedure that feeds trajectories and metric evaluations to an LLM, replacing human prompt editing in the main demonstration. The previously described rejection-fine-tuning application is removed.

E1.justification: The represented environments and task coverage remain: CoGym, Sotopia, WebArena, WebVoyager, Baba-Is-AI, MiniHack, and NNetNav-Live metric induction. The new Gemini experiment uses the retained Baba-Is-AI benchmark. MiniHack experiments and NNetNav-Live induced metrics remain in the appendices; removing the web fine-tuning application changes procedures and results within retained web-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Section 5.2 reports comparison against goal-completion LLM-as-a-Judge rejection fine-tuning; that comparison disappears in v3. Expert-defined evaluation categories in Table 2 and the earlier game-agent baseline comparisons remain. The new leaderboard figures provide contextual comparisons, without establishing additional controlled comparator evaluations.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a substantially different main optimization experiment: Gemini-2.5-Flash supplies the agent, AutoLibra processing, and prompt optimizer. Three feedback stages contain repeated LLM prompt updates using one trajectory per selected task, whereas v2 describes human prompt engineering and iteration transitions based on metric improvement. The NNetNav-Live rejection-fine-tuning protocol is removed; earlier appendix protocols remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds qualitative analysis of skills emerging during automated optimization, including map-boundary recognition, win-rule formation, self-referential rules, and a late performance dip attributed to overthinking. The behavior-example ablation, now Figure 3, and the earlier Baba-Is-AI and MiniHack error analyses remain substantially unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 adds uncertainty ranges to its quoted Baba-Is-AI leaderboard context, including 50.8% ± 4.6% and 56.7% ± 4.5%, whereas v2 quotes point baselines. This is limited to attributed benchmark results: Table 1's 40-instance validation and confidence intervals remain unchanged, and no new repeated-run or uncertainty procedure is documented for the Gemini experiment.

E6.justification: v3 adds Gemini optimization curves, five plus five plus one newly induced metrics, a reported 20% success-rate improvement, and a late performance dip. These use different model and optimization conditions from v2. The web fine-tuning results in v2 Table 3, including success rates increasing from 34.8% to 39.7%, disappear. Tables 1–2 and the earlier game results retained in the appendices are unchanged.

T1.justification: The aspect and metric definitions, positive/negative/not-applicable scoring, coverage and redundancy definitions, and appendix pseudocode remain equivalent. Neither version adds or removes substantive formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The application contributions are redefined. v2 explicitly claims superiority over task-success targets for prompt engineering and demonstrates web-agent fine-tuning. v3 instead emphasizes automatic prompt optimization and self-regulated improvement, while its conclusion limits demonstrated learning to non-parametric improvement. The central contribution of inducing interpretable evaluation metrics remains.

C2.justification: v3 removes the Broader Impact Statement's explicit limitations concerning text-only agents, author-annotator diversity, untested annotator-experience effects, and LLM biases. New Section 8 develops a broader social-learning and knowledge-transfer interpretation. Section 5 also adds explanations linking induced metrics to Gemini skill development and overthinking; earlier appendix failure conditions remain.

D1.justification: v3 describes Gemini's roles and trajectory-based prompt-update inputs, but removes v2's NNetNav-Live sourcing, post-hoc task labeling, Llama-8b-nnetnav-live, and top-10% selection recipe. Code and data links and older game prompts remain unchanged. Appendix C still specifies GPT-4o-241120 for all experiments and does not provide corresponding Gemini optimizer prompts.

R1.justification: v3 removes the introduction's goal-oriented versus behavioral evaluation survey and associated citations, and drops the NNetNav reference. It adds Humphrey (1976) for social intelligence and Gemini Team (2025). The dedicated related-work section and the core positioning relative to thematic analysis and LLooM remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: the introduction is shortened, Section 5's two application subsections become a new automated-optimization account, and the Broader Impact Statement is replaced by The Bigger Picture. A main contents list is added, the title drops AI, and explanations and headings are edited throughout.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different page template, typography, headers, and table-caption layout. Four method diagrams move from the main text to Appendix A. The dual-application improvement diagram is replaced by a stage-based plot, a new Baba-Is-AI illustration is added, and v2's main Tables 3–4 are removed. Retained appendix displays are reflowed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The automated Gemini demonstration adds useful evidence and v3 narrows some comparative claims. However, its main experiment lacks matching appendix documentation: Section 5 uses Gemini while Appendix C still specifies GPT-4o for all experiments. Removing the web fine-tuning comparison and explicit bias and applicability limitations also reduces evidential breadth and qualification. With the core validation and earlier appendix studies preserved, these shortcomings produce a limited overall decline in coherence and reproducibility.
